title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 35
paragraphs: These barbarians, I say, took their way in this direction; but others of them, with guides, had set out to go to the temple at Delphi, keeping Parnassos on their right. All the parts of Phokis over which these marched they ravaged; for they set fire to the towns of Panopeus, Daulis, and Aiolis. The reason they marched separately from the rest of the army in this direction was in order to plunder the temple at Delphi and deliver its treasures over to King Xerxes. Xerxes was well acquainted with everything of note in it — better, I am told, than with the things he had left in his own house at home — since many were constantly reporting them to him, especially the votive offerings of Croesus son of Alyattes.
